reason: Confirmed, but the severity is inflated for this branch. I bundled apps/web/src/core/api.ts with the repo's esbuild and ran `apply`: a state with findings [f1] plus a `session.snapshot` that holds the reply step 'Recorded one finding for x' gives 'findings [ f1 ] steps 1'. The snapshot branch is `{ ...state, snapshot: event.snapshot }`, so the findings stay as they were. SessionSnapshot has no findings field. The fetch effect in Session.tsx (lines 77-104) depends on `[sessionId, projectId]` only, and no other code reads `${base}/findings`. openStream (api.ts 200-203) never replays missed events, and `finding.recorded` is the only later source. The scenario is reachable: demoWorker.ts 65-69 records a finding and then appends the reply step, so a socket drop in that window leaves the FINDINGS panel and its count short until a full page load. Sharpened scenario: the page loses only a `finding.recorded` that the server sends while the socket is down. A finding recorded before the first fetch is safe because of the merge at lines 92-97. Severity: Session.tsx is not in this diff and the behaviour is the same on origin/main. The claim that this branch 'makes the mismatch show' is weak, because the 'Recorded one finding' reply text came through the snapshot before this branch too. The effect is a stale side panel after a rare network drop, with no data loss and no wrong money. It is a valid follow-up (read the findings again when the stream goes to 'open') and does not block this branch.
